newsitem.title: CONGO: Rebel group tells investors leave Angola's Cabinda.
newsitem.headline: Rebel group tells investors leave Angola's Cabinda.

text.p: An armed group fighting for independence in Angola's oil-rich Cabinda enclave has warned foreign investors there to leave immediately.

A spokesman for the armed wing of the Front for the Liberation of the Cabinda Enclave (FLEC-FAC) told a news conference in Congo's capital the group had the means to destroy their economic installations.
"The responsibility for the consequences of ignoring this ultimatum will rest with those concerned and the Angolan government, which has put the foreign investors in Cabinda," Emmanuel N'Zita said.

N'Zita, son of FLEC-FAC leader Henriques Tiago N'Zita, who lives in France, said oil companies protected by Angolan forces would be targeted and the group had knocked out the air defence system at Malongo refinery.
Apart from oil companies such as Chevron, ELF, AGIP and Angola's SONAGOL, he said the warning applied to about 40 companies including a Malaysian wood company and Portuguese construction companies.
"We are obliged to hit these foreign companies because they are supporting Angola's policy in our territory, Cabinda, which we want (to see) independent," he said.
Cabinda, a former Portuguese protectorate, became an Angolan province in 1975.
